articles.summary: In-store grocery shoppers show stronger loyalty than consumers who also shop online, often sticking to fewer retailers each month. Research shows omnichannel shoppers spread their spending across significantly more brands, making retention more challenging for retailers. Businesses that deliver seamless, value-driven experiences across physical and digital touchpoints gain a clear advantage, and solutions like VenHub help bridge this gap by connecting convenience, technology, and in-store engagement.
articles.title: In-Store Shoppers Are More Loyal Than Online-Only Consumers

articles.title: VenHub Global New Location In Hollywood Featured on LA Times

articles.summary: Frictionless payment and skipping the checkout line are quickly becoming everyday expectations for grocery shoppers. Scan & Go delivers this convenience through contactless shopping, faster trips, and helpful in-app features like digital lists and product information. VenHub is best suited for this practice, offering a fully autonomous, frictionless retail experience built for modern consumer expectations.
articles.title: Shoppers Expect Frictionless Checkout

articles.summary: As consumer expectations continue to evolve, 60% of consumers say they want easier access to self-service solutions that allow them to resolve issues quickly and independently. This growing preference reflects demand for speed, convenience, and intuitive digital experiences across industries. Businesses that invest in seamless self-service tools can better meet customer needs while improving efficiency and satisfaction.
articles.title: 60% of Consumers Want Easier Access to Self-Service Solutions

articles.summary: Some scientists are reportedly embedding hidden AI prompts in academic papers to influence automated or AI-assisted peer reviews toward more positive feedback. These concealed instructions raise concerns about transparency, ethics, and the integrity of the research review process. The issue highlights growing challenges as AI becomes more involved in academic publishing and evaluation.
articles.title: Scientists Reportedly Hiding AI Text Prompts in Academic Papers to Receive Positive Peer Reviews
